chats.answer:
For a weekend trip, I'd look for a portable power station weighing under 10 lb, with at least 250–300 Wh of battery capacity and a USB-C port supporting 100W Power Delivery (PD).

The important distinction is that 100W USB-C is charging speed, not battery capacity. A 300Wh power station can typically provide around 240–270Wh of usable energy through USB-C, enough for roughly 3–4 full charges of a 60Wh laptop battery.

If you're working continuously at 100W, however, that same station will last only about 2.5 hours. For intermittent weekend laptop use, it's a much better fit.

Will 288Wh last a weekend?

Assuming about 250Wh usable through USB-C:

Average laptop draw

	

Total powered runtime




20W — light work

	

~12.5 hours




40W — normal work

	

~6.3 hours




60W — demanding work

	

~4.2 hours




100W — sustained heavy load

	

~2.5 hours

These estimates exclude the laptop's own battery, so your total working time could be longer.

I'd choose the Anker C300 DC or EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC for the best balance of weight, capacity, and high-wattage USB-C.

One question: Which laptop are you charging — MacBook Pro 14/16, Windows laptop, or something else? That will help determine whether 288Wh is enough for your entire weekend without recharging.
